item.title: Threshold and Below-Threshold Dynamics for the Energy-Critical NLS: The Higher-Kinetic-Energy Regime
item.description: arXiv:2610.22447v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the focusing energy-critical nonlinear Schr\"odinger equation below and at the ground-state energy, focusing on solutions in the upper energy cone, characterized by \[ E(u)\le E(W),\qquad \|\nabla u\|_{L_x^2}>\|\nabla W\|_{L_x^2}, \] where \(W\) is the ground state. Unlike the lower cone, where compactness of critical solutions plays a central role in understanding the dynamics, such compactness is generally unavailable on the upper branch. Consequently, previous results have often required additional assumptions, such as finite mass or finite variance. In this paper, we remove the finite-mass assumption in the radial setting and give a complete characterization of the upper-cone dynamics in the natural energy space \(\dot H^1_{\mathrm{rad}}\), resolving an open problem posed by Duyckaerts and Merle\cite{DM08}. In particular, this establishes finite-time blow-up of the special threshold solution \(W^+\) in the negative time direction in dimensions \(d=3,4\). For non-radial data in dimensions \(d\ge5\), we show that {for solutions in the interior of the upper cone, the limit superior of their $\dot H^1$-norm satisfies an explicit lower bound as time approaches each endpoint of the maximal lifespan,} while forward-global solutions on the upper threshold sheet that remain below this level must coincide with \(W^+\) modulo symmetries. We also obtain a complete classification of upper-threshold dynamics for finite-variance data in all dimensions \(d\ge3\).
item.dc:creator: Zuyu Ma, Changxing Miao, Kai Yang, Xiaoyi Zhang, Jiqiang Zheng

item.title: Well-posedness of 2D stochastic parabolic-parabolic Keller-Segel system with logistic source
item.description: arXiv:2610.22458v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider a stochastic, fully parabolic Keller-Segel system with multiplicative noise in non-divergence form and a logistic source in a two-dimensional bounded domain, subject to random initial data. We construct a global-in-time, non-negative martingale solution by means of a suitable regularisation procedure, combined with Banach fixed-point arguments, a localisation procedure, and a stochastic compactness method. We further establish pathwise uniqueness and uniqueness in law for martingale solutions, and prove the existence of a unique global-in-time, non-negative weak solution without imposing any smallness condition on the initial data.
item.dc:creator: Erika Hausenblas, Boris Jidjou Moghomye, Paul Andre Razafimandimby

item.title: Admissible solutions of the Euler equations
item.description: arXiv:2610.22491v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we prove the existence of an extensive class of initial data--characterized by intermittency dimension and roughness--for which the d-dimensional Euler equations (d \ge 2) admit a decreasing energy channel with infinitely many admissible solutions arising from the same initial data. This class includes initial data in C^{1-\kappa}(\mathbb{T}^d) and W^{1,p}(\mathbb{T}^d) for any 0 < \kappa < 1 and 2 < p < \infty, thereby demonstrating the sharpness of the Lions and Yudovich uniqueness principles. Our proof is based on a new backward convex integration scheme employing approximate \Lambda-Euler equations to reduce the initial error and on uncovering a quantitative relationship between regularity, energy, and intermittency.
item.dc:creator: Alexey Cheskidov, Zirong Zeng, Deng Zhang

item.title: A new proof of equality cases of the Brunn-Minkowski inequality on manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2610.22517v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We give a new proof of equality cases of the Brunn-Minkowski inequality on manifolds, following the work of Balogh-Kris\'atly. Our proof extends also to equality cases of the strong Brunn-Minkowski inequality, introduced by Magnabosco-Portinale-Rossi.
item.dc:creator: Osama Farooqui

item.title: Solvability of complex Hessian equations corresponding to right-Noetherian polynomials
item.description: arXiv:2610.22524v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: On compact Hermitian manifolds, we establish a framework using radial normalization for the solvability of complex Hessian equation in form type, corresponding to right-Noetherian polynomials whose coefficients may not be constant functions. The solvability of a radial normalized equation is characterized by the existence of a C-subsolution at radial slope, which extends the results of Guo-Song to this setting.
item.dc:creator: Junbang Liu, Yulun Xu

item.title: Hardy-Sobolev-Maz'ya Inequalities for $\boldsymbol{1<p<2}$
item.description: arXiv:2610.22540v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish Hardy--Sobolev--Maz'ya inequalities in the subquadratic range $1<p<2$ for singularities supported on affine subspaces and for arbitrary domains. We first prove a Hardy--Sobolev--Maz'ya inequality for singularities supported on affine subspaces of arbitrary codimension $1\leq k<N$, showing that the deficit in the sharp Hardy inequality controls a suitable weighted Sobolev norm. Combining the same convexity estimate with the one-dimensional approach of Frank and Loss in [9], we also establish Hardy--Sobolev--Maz'ya inequalities on arbitrary domains with the mean distance to the boundary and thereby solve a problem posed in [9]. These results complete the previously unresolved subquadratic range $1<p<2$ and, together with the known results for $p\geq 2$, provide a unified Hardy--Sobolev--Maz'ya theory for all $1<p<N$ associated with plane singularities and general domains.
item.dc:creator: Avas Banerjee, Micha{\l} Kijaczko, Vivek Sahu

item.title: Geometric rigidity principles for $\mathscr{A}$-free Young measures
item.description: arXiv:2610.22560v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study generalized Young measures generated by $\mathscr{A}$-free measures, $\mathscr{A}$ a constant-rank operator, in a compactification of the value space adapted to an energy. Given an $\mathscr{A}$-quasiconvex integrand $G$ of linear growth with coercive recession function $G^\infty$, the unit sphere at infinity is replaced by the indicatrix $\mathbb{S}_G=\{G^\infty=1\}$, which need be neither convex nor symmetric. The two compactifications are equivalent, but in the adapted one the equality cases of the Jensen inequalities characterizing $\mathscr{A}$-free Young measures become statements of convex geometry about $\mathbb{S}_G$. We prove the characterization in this setting, with a new streamlined proof of the inhomogenization step based on a dyadic martingale argument. We then show that if $\mathscr{A}$-free measures $\mu_j\overset{*}{\rightharpoonup}\mu$ and their $G$-energies converge, then at $|\mu^s|$-almost every point the concentration-angle measure is supported on the smallest exposed face of $\overline{\mathrm{co}}(\mathbb{S}_G)$ containing the $G$-polar of $\mu^s$; in particular, it never charges the set where $G^\infty$ differs from its convex envelope, which, by the automatic convexity of Kirchheim and Kristensen, does not meet the wave cone. The concentration on the singular part of $\mu$ is elementary for every such sequence if and only if each point of the wave cone on $\mathbb{S}_G$ is an extreme point of $\overline{\mathrm{co}}(\mathbb{S}_G)$, as for the Euclidean norm underlying Reshetnyak's continuity theorem; on flat faces of $\mathbb{S}_G$, rigidity degrades from a point to a face. Finally, we prove a transfer principle for the convergence of energies of $\mathrm{BV}$ maps under Dirichlet boundary conditions.
item.dc:creator: Sergio Scalabrino

item.title: On the two critical exponents for a dispersive equation with weak dissipation
item.description: arXiv:2610.22616v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we study a nonlinear Cauchy problem written in normal form \begin{equation*} \begin{cases} u_{tt} + A u+ Bu_t =D|u|^\alpha, & t\geq 0, x \in \mathbb{R}^n\\ u(0,x)=u_0(x),\,u_t(0,x)=u_1(x). \end{cases} \end{equation*} Here~ $Af=\mathscr{F}^{-1}(a(\xi)^2\mathscr{F}f)$, with $a(\xi)$ homogeneous of order $k > 0$ under the assumption that the Hessian matrix of $a(\xi)$ is nonsingular, the operator $Bf=\mathscr{F}^{-1}(b(\xi)\mathscr{F}f)$ represents a weak dissipation, in the sense that $b(\xi) \sim 1$ as $|\xi| \to \infty$ and %, in several models, $D=B$ but we also consider the case $Df=\nu\ast (-\Delta)^\delta(I-\Delta)^{-\delta}$, with $\nu$ a bounded measure and $\delta \geq k/2$. We derive $L^p-L^q$ estimates of the linear solution operator to the considered model and we prove the transition from a Fujita-type exponent to a Strauss-type exponent for the global-in-time existence of small data solution for the corresponding nonlinear problems.
item.dc:creator: Marcello D'Abbicco, Antonio Lagioia

item.title: Double interaction principle for the Lorentz force equation
item.description: arXiv:2610.22627v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper we study the Lorentz force equation using the Poincare action functional. We show that, if the scalar electric potential has good interactions at infinity and around the origin with the vector magnetic potential, then the Lorentz force equation has at least two periodic solutions with a fixed period. For the proof of our main result we introduce a new minimax theorem for the Poincare action functional that does not require the Palais-Smale compactness condition and provides the existence of twin critical points. The interaction at infinity in the electromagnetic potential implies a weak compactness property of the Poincare action functional, while the interaction around the origin gives the separation property of the functional.
item.dc:creator: Cristain Bereanu, Nicusor Costea

item.title: Probabilistic Fourier extension and the Schr\"odinger equation
item.description: arXiv:2610.22634v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We give applications of the probabilistic Fourier extension theorem for the paraboloid in d dimensions (see [Saw7] for the sphere, and the proof there holds for a smooth compact piece of the paraboloid) to the global initial value problem for the Schr\"odinger equation with initial data f, in which we obtain sharp averaged Sobolev regularity results over certain `martingale transforms' of the intial data f. The deterministic analogue in three dimensions has been obtained recently by OpenAI [Ope].
item.dc:creator: Lyudmila Korobenko, Eric T. Sawyer

item.title: Spectral stability for strong ideal-gas shock layers
item.description: arXiv:2610.22660v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We give a purely analytical proof of one-dimensional spectral stability of sufficiently strong shock layers for the full ideal-gas Navier--Stokes equations with constant viscosity and heat conduction. Earlier work reduced this question to a limiting problem and gave numerical evidence of stability, but no proof. We prove stability on an explicit region of gas constants and transport ratios that includes air and monatomic gases. No step of the argument relies on numerical computation, and the arguments, taking the cited results of Humpherys, Lyng, and Zumbrun as hypotheses, have also been verified in the Lean proof assistant.
item.dc:creator: Jeffrey Humpherys

item.title: The fractional H\'enon-Lane-Emden conjecture and some critical nonexistence phenomena
item.description: arXiv:2610.22802v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We refine the proof method for the H\'enon-Lane-Emden system and extend it to fractional orders $0<s<1$, proving subcritical nonexistence of positive classical solutions. And we find examples with $0<s<1/2$ and fixed nonzero weights for which existence and nonexistence occur at different points of the same critical hyperbola.
item.dc:creator: Kui Li, Haoyang Lu, Zhitao Zhang

item.title: Integral Volume Criteria for Semilinear and Quasilinear Liouville Theorems on Complete Manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2610.22803v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $M$ be a connected complete noncompact Riemannian manifold without boundary, and let $V_o(R)$ denote its ball volume. We prove Liouville theorems without any curvature assumption. For $p>1$ and $q>p-1$, divergence of $\int^\infty R^{pq/(p-1)-1}V_o(R)^{-(q-p+1)/(p-1)}\dd R$ forces every nonnegative Sobolev weak supersolution of $-\Delta_pu\ge u^q$ to vanish. For $q>\max\{1,p-1\}$, divergence of $\int^\infty R^{p-1}V_o(R)^{-(q-p+1)}\dd R$ forces every nonnegative global distributional energy supersolution of $u_t-\Delta_pu\ge u^q$ to vanish. Consequently, the corresponding Cauchy problem has no global solution in this class with a nonzero nonnegative local $L^1$ initial trace.
item.dc:creator: Yongheng Qin, Yuhua Sun

item.title: Exact lattice resonances and a sharp second Picard obstruction for the two-dimensional inviscid primitive equations
item.description: arXiv:2610.22853v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study periodic perturbations of a rest state with constant stable stratification for the two-dimensional non-rotating primitive equations without viscosity or thermal diffusion on a fixed rectangular torus. Fourier resonance analysis and Sobolev estimates show that, despite unitary linear evolution, the polarized second Picard operator admits no bilinear bound losing less than one derivative at any Sobolev order and any fixed nonzero time for real data with zero vertical means. The loss is sharp for \(s\ge2\), with matching bounds on every sufficiently high physical dyadic shell. We classify exact lattice resonances in all signed channels and compute their polarized coefficients. A mixed-branch family with fixed vertical frequencies isolates diagnostic transport and shows that finite vertical regularity cannot reduce the loss below one horizontal derivative in tensor-product Sobolev spaces. In contrast, for \(s\ge2\), the horizontal mean of the second Picard operator admits a time-uniform one-derivative bound. In interaction variables, the response divided by time converges to the resonant operator, with an \(O(|t|^{-1})\) error after a four-derivative loss for \(s\ge4\). Finally, among real linear spaces defined solely by a common Fourier-support constraint on both components, the maximal spaces on which the full nonlinearity vanishes for all smooth states are precisely those supported on primitive lattice rays. On these rays, we construct explicit global solutions and obtain an exact criterion for uniform strict stratification.
item.dc:creator: Fengjie Luo, Zhengdong Du

item.title: Riemann problem for the isentropic Cargo-LeRoux system with extended Chaplygin fluids
item.description: arXiv:2610.22950v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This study deals with the Riemann solutions of the isentropic Cargo-LeRoux system of conservation laws along with an extended Chaplygin fluid model and a generalized equation of state that captures nonlinear compressibility and non-ideal fluid behavior. It is shown that in the vanishing pressure limiting case, the Riemann solution yields a delta shock and a vacuum state. Delta shocks form when mass concentrates due to vanishing pressure, while vacuum states emerge in the rarefaction-dominated regions. These wave patterns are crucial in modeling real-world problems like discontinuous and multi-phase astrophysical fluid flows, underwater explosions, and combustion fronts.
item.dc:creator: Priyanka, M. Zafar, V. D. Sharma

item.title: Asymptotic stability of Bloch wall for dispersive Landau-Lifshitz equation
item.description: arXiv:2610.22978v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider the Bloch wall stationary solutions to the dispersive Landau-Lifshitz equation with Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction (DMI). First, we establish a dichotomy for the orbital stability and instability depending on the value of a coupling constant. Then, under symmetric perturbations, we prove that the Bloch wall is asymptotically stable in the energetically favorable regime.
item.dc:creator: Slim Ibrahim, Christof Melcher, Ikkei Shimizu

item.title: Liouville theorems for $-\Delta_{m,g}u=\lambda e^u|\nabla u|^q$ in the full range of gradient exponents
item.description: arXiv:2610.23029v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the equation \[ -\Delta_{m,g}u=\lambda e^u|\nabla u|^q \] on complete, connected, noncompact Riemannian manifolds of dimension $n\ge2$ with $\Ric_g\ge0$. For every $m>1$, $q\in\mathbb R$ and $\lambda>0$, we prove that every positive $C^1$ weak solution is constant when $q>0$, while no such solution exists when $q\le0$. For $q>m$, we derive a local gradient estimate independent of the solution by Nash--Moser iteration, which leads to automatic boundedness and resolves the question raised by Lu and Zhu~\cite[Remark~1.6(B)]{LZ}. For $m-1<q<m$, we use an auxiliary function and a divergence inequality to extend the Liouville result beyond the range covered by existing gradient-inequality methods. The remaining cases are treated by suitable changes of variables and integral estimates. The conclusions also extend to real-valued solutions bounded below.
item.dc:creator: Yuhua Sun, Zhen Wang, Mengyu Zhang

item.title: Isolated singularities of weak solutions to the Serrin-critical $p$-Laplace equation
item.description: arXiv:2610.23045v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We classify isolated singularities of nonnegative weak solutions to the Serrin-critical quasilinear Lane-Emden equation $-\Delta_p u=u^{\frac{n(p-1)}{n-p}}$ in $B_1\setminus\{0\}$, where $1<p<n$, $\Delta_p$ is the classical $p$-Laplacian operator and $B_1\setminus\{0\}\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ is the punctured unit ball. We prove that either the origin is a removable singularity or $u$ satisfies $\lim_{x\to0}|x|^{\frac{n-p}{p-1}}(\log\frac1{|x|})^{\frac{n-p}{p(p-1)}}u(x)=[\frac{n-p}{p}(\frac{n-p}{p-1})^{p-1}]^{\frac{n-p}{p(p-1)}}$. This extends the result of Aviles (Comm. Math. Phys. 1987: 177--192) from the semilinear case $p=2$ to the full range $1<p<n$, without assuming radial symmetry. We develop a new BV-based argument for weak solutions. We also give a direct construction of positive radial singular solutions with the same asymptotic behavior.
item.dc:creator: Meiqing Xu, Hui Yang

item.title: Sharp improved Sobolev inequalities on $\mathbb{S}^n$
item.description: arXiv:2610.23069v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove sharp improved Sobolev inequalities on $\mathbb{S}^n$, $n\ge 4$, for functions whose critical density $|u|^{2n/(n-2)}$ has zero barycenter, without any symmetry assumption. The Dirichlet coefficient improves by the optimal factor $2^{-2/n}$, while the coefficient of the $L^2$ term remains one. Equality holds precisely for constant functions. This establishes the sharp form of Aubin's improved Sobolev inequality in every dimension $n\ge4$.
item.dc:creator: Juncheng Wei, Zetian Yan, Zikai Ye

item.title: Global well-posedness for the compressible Navier--Stokes equations in 3D bounded domains under a new smallness condition
item.description: arXiv:2610.23091v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate the three-dimensional barotropic compressible Navier--Stokes equations involving vacuum in a bounded domain with Navier-slip boundary conditions. It is shown that such a model admits a unique global strong solution provided the gradient of the initial velocity and the initial pressure deviation are suitably small in $L^2$. In particular, \textit{the smallness threshold depends only on the known parameters and the prescribed density bounds.} Our result provides a new analytical framework for the global well-posedness theory of the compressible Navier--Stokes equations.
item.dc:creator: Lin Xu, Xin Zhong

item.title: Linearization in nonlocal elasticity via Gamma-convergence
item.description: arXiv:2610.23114v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Linearization is a classical tool in continuum mechanics that connects nonlinear models of solids to their linear counterparts through the small-strain limit, as in the passage from finite to linear elasticity. Here, we study a nonlocal analogue of this limit process in the context of state-based peridynamics, starting from a class of models in nonlocal hyperelasticity subject to nonlocal Dirichlet boundary conditions. Recent formal calculations in the literature indicate that the linearized versions of these models are closely related to the widely used Eringen models. The main purpose of this note is to make this connection rigorous by establishing $\Gamma$-convergence of the associated energy functionals and a corresponding compactness result that together imply strong convergence of minimizers. Our proof relies on a local-to-nonlocal transfer argument that reduces the problem to a well-known local linearization result.
item.dc:creator: Carolin Kreisbeck, Carlos Mora-Corral, Felix Seifert

item.title: Degenerated scalar balance laws: stability of the critical wave
item.description: arXiv:2610.23115v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider scalar balance laws whith degenerated growth function at one infinity. It is the transition point between monostable and bistable waves. We find it admits smooth profiles arising from both settings, and show stability for the slowest of these waves, under a sign assumption on the flux. The presence of a characteristic point at infinity weaken the temporal decay: an exponential spatial localization loss is necessary to get algebraic temporal decay.
item.dc:creator: Louis Gar\'enaux

item.title: Singular Stochastic Heat Equations with Fractional Memory
item.description: arXiv:2610.23189v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We extend the paracontrolled distribution approach of Gubinelli, Imkeller, and Perkowski to singular stochastic heat equations with Caputo fractional time derivatives. By establishing Schauder estimates for the time-fractional heat flow and controlling history terms, we address the difficulties arising from temporal memory and the lack of the semigroup property. For the one-dimensional rough Burgers-type equation driven by space-time white noise with spatial dissipation \((-\Delta)^\sigma\), we prove global well-posedness for \(\sigma\in(5/6,1]\) and \(\nu\in(6\sigma/(12\sigma-5),1]\). For the heat equation with nonlinear multiplicative spatial white noise on the two-dimensional torus, we establish local well-posedness of renormalized solutions and an \(L^\infty\) blow-up criterion for every \(\nu\in(0,1]\).
item.dc:creator: Shuolin Zhang, \quad Zhaoyang Yin

item.title: Solutions to the Fokker-Planck equation with time-dependent force and source in $\mathbb R^3$
item.description: arXiv:2610.23191v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper concerns the global solutions of the kinetic Fokker-Planck (KFP) equation in $\mathbb R^3$ driven by a given external force $E=E(t,x)$ and an inhomogeneous source term $S_0=S_0(t,x,v)$. First, when $E$ and $S_0$ are sufficiently small in a suitable hybrid homogeneous Besov-Sobolev framework without any time-decay assumption, we establish the global well-posedness of the Cauchy problem in the hybrid homogeneous space $L_v^2(\dot B^{ {1}/{2}}_{2,\infty}(\mathbb R^3_x) \cap\dot H^N(\mathbb R^3_x))$ with $N\geq 3$. We further obtain the uniform stability of the Cauchy problem via semi-group theory and a refined energy method. Second, when both $E$ and $S_0$ are time-periodic of the period $T$, we show the existence of time-periodic solutions with the same period $T$ and their asymptotic stability as $t\to \infty$. Moreover, we derive the time-decay estimate of the perturbation around time-periodic solutions for initial data in $L^p$-norm with $ {3}/{2}< p \leq 2$. Finally, when both $E$ and $S_0$ are independent of $t$, we establish the existence of stationary solutions and their asymptotic stability. Our results provide a unified treatment of time-periodic dynamics and stationary states for the KFP equation with small force and source terms.
item.dc:creator: Renjun Duan, Fucai Li, Jinkai Ni, Zhu Zhang

item.title: Rough Stochastic Viscous Camassa-Holm equation
item.description: arXiv:2610.23198v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we establish well-posedness results for the viscous Camassa--Holm equation driven by the additive Gaussian noise $(1-\partial_x^2)^{-\eta}\xi$, where $\xi$ denotes the space-time white noise and $\eta>-1/12$. This formulation includes spatially colored noise for $\eta>0$, space-time white noise for $\eta=0$, and rough noise for $-1/12<\eta<0$. More precisely, we establish a pathwise solution theory via approximation by equations driven by regularized noises. The main difficulty arises from the singular interactions between the nonlinear terms and the irregular stochastic convolution. By introducing suitable enhanced stochastic objects and applying paracontrolled techniques, we obtain local well-posedness for the full range $\eta>-1/12$. Furthermore, when $\eta>1/4$, we establish global well-posedness by deriving suitable energy estimates.
item.dc:creator: Xiaoxin Chen, Yiyao Lian, Zhaoyang Yin, Shuolin Zhang

item.title: Harnack-type inequalities for nonlocal doubly nonlinear parabolic equations
item.description: arXiv:2610.23261v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish intrinsic Harnack inequalities for nonlocal doubly nonlinear parabolic equations in the slow-diffusion range: \begin{equation*} (u^q)_t+ \operatorname{P.V.} \int\limits_{\mathbb{R}^N}\frac{|u(x, t)-u(y, t)|^{p-2}(u(x, t)-u(y, t))}{|x-y|^{N+sp}}\,dy=0,\quad s\in(0,1),\quad 0<q < p-1. \end{equation*}
item.dc:creator: Mariia Savchenko, Igor Skrypnik, Yevgeniia Yevgenieva

item.title: Nonlocal-to-local variational limits of energies on partitions
item.description: arXiv:2610.23389v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study, through a $\Gamma$-convergence procedure, the asymptotic behaviour of a general class of nonlocal energies defined on functions taking values in a finite set $Y=\{y_1,\dots,y_N\}\subset\mathbb R^m$. These energies are written in terms of double integrals accounting for pairwise interactions in an open set $\Omega$, weighted by a kernel $K_\varepsilon$. If the latter is controlled from above and below by suitable non-negative radial kernels with unit mass concentrating at the origin, then, up to subsequences, the $\Gamma$-limit has domain $BV(\Omega;Y)$ and is given by a local surface energy. We show that the locality of the $\Gamma$-limit is not guaranteed if the concentration of mass fails. For a class of reference energies, we obtain a more explicit representation of the limit energy, also for non-radial kernels, recovering the limits of isotropic and anisotropic fractional perimeters. We also prove a homogenization result for periodic kernels.
item.dc:creator: Roberto Alicandro, Giuliana Fusco, Chiara Leone

item.title: Minimum-Area Enclosing Rectangles and the First Neumann Eigenvalue of Planar Convex Domains
item.description: arXiv:2610.23439v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $\Omega$ be a bounded convex domain in the plane and let $R$ be a minimum-area rectangle containing $\overline\Omega$. We prove that if the ratio of the shorter side of $R$ to its longer side is at most $\rho \approx 0.443485$, then the first nonzero Neumann eigenvalue of $\Omega$ is bounded from below by that of $R$. Moreover, equality holds if and only if $\Omega$ coincides with the interior of $R$. The proof is based on a flux identity for the means of a test function over vertical sections of $\Omega$, combined with weighted estimates involving the distributional second derivatives of the boundary functions. Finally, we show that the threshold $\rho\approx0.443485$ is nearly optimal by constructing, for every ratio in $(0.457994,1/2)$, trapezoids that are arbitrarily close to their minimum-area enclosing rectangle and for which the inequality fails.
item.dc:creator: Xiaolong Li, Jin Sun, Kui Wang

item.title: Reconnection in 2D Inertial Magnetohydrodynamics
item.description: arXiv:2610.23494v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider two-fluid equations of inertial magnetohydrodynamics in two spatial dimensions. These equations can be recast as the evolution of two active scalars, with fluid-like interaction kernels. The equations come in two flavors, left-handed and right-handed. They are conservative and have global unique solutions for both smooth initial data and for initial data in Yudovich class $L^1(\mathbb R^2)\cap L^{\infty}(\mathbb R^2)$. We prove that the inviscid limit holds in Yudovich class. We prove the persistence of $C^{2,\alpha}$ regularity of patch boundaries through merger events for the left-handed equations. We finally show numerical examples of magnetic reconnection, validating known rigorous results and uncovering new cases.
item.dc:creator: Lydia Boubendir, Peter Constantin, Hezekiah Grayer II, Zhongtian Hu

item.title: Classification of boundary blow-ups for the Mumford-Shah functional with Dirichlet boundary conditions
item.description: arXiv:2610.23513v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We classify boundary blow-ups of minimizers of the Mumford-Shah functional on bounded planar domains with Dirichlet boundary conditions. At every point where the discontinuity set meets the boundary of the domain, we prove that the discontinuity set of each blow-up is the tangent line to the boundary at that point. This settles the conjecture formulated by the author in 2024.
item.dc:creator: Francesco Deangelis

item.title: Gaussian measures under the Navier-Stokes and heat flows are mutually singular
item.description: arXiv:2610.23591v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider the incompressible Navier-Stokes equations on the torus $\mathbb{T}^d$, $d \ge 2$, with translation invariant Gaussian random initial data. We show that, for the Gaussian measure formally given by $\mu_0 \sim \exp(-\frac12 \| u \|_{\dot H^\alpha}^2)$ on divergence-free fields, its nonlinear evolution $\nu_t$ and its linear evolution $\mu_t$ are mutually singular for almost every time. Moreover, the same holds for the nonlinear evolution of an arbitrary initial measure $\nu_0$. This is in sharp contrast to the available results for Hamiltonian PDEs, where Gaussian measures are commonly quasi-invariant. We achieve this by showing that there exists a set $\mathscr G_t$ such that $\mu_t(\mathscr G_t) = 1$, but for any smooth solution of Navier-Stokes, the set of times $t$ such that $u(t) \in \mathscr G_t$ is null, which we deduce from a quantitative convexity bound for frequency-localised versions of the (typically infinite) quantity $\| \mathrm{e}^{-t \Delta} u(t) \|_{L^2}^2$.
item.dc:creator: Niko Nikov, Leonardo Tolomeo

item.title: Faber--Krahn inequality for homogeneous normalized $p$-Laplacian type operators
item.description: arXiv:2610.23593v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish a sharp Faber-Krahn inequality for the normalized (or game-theoretic) $p$-Laplacian, proving that, for $p\geq 2$, the ball uniquely minimizes the principal Dirichlet eigenvalue among bounded connected Lipschitz domains of prescribed volume satisfying a uniform exterior sphere condition. More generally, we prove the same inequality for the family of homogeneous operators $|Du|^\gamma\Delta_p^N u$, with $p>1$ and $-1<\gamma\le p-2$. Unlike the classical $p$-Laplacian, these operators lack a variational structure, preventing the use of standard symmetrization arguments. Our proof overcomes this difficulty through a level-set approach: it relies on a flux identity for the eigenvalue, for which a variational interpretation re-emerges in the special case where the domain is a ball.
item.dc:creator: Graziano Crasta, Ilaria Fragal\`a

item.title: Sharp maximum estimates for linear uniformly elliptic equations with measurable coefficients
item.description: arXiv:2610.23596v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper we obtain sharp exponents in the Aleksandrov-Bakelman-Pucci maximum estimate for linear uniformly elliptic equations with measurable coefficients, originally conjectured by Pucci in 1966 \cite{Pucci}, together with corresponding sharp results under the more natural quantification of uniform ellipticity in more than two dimensions. The proofs combine a Hessian integral inequality obtained from boundary Morse inequalities with an obstacle argument. The estimates also hold on arbitrary open sets, of finite volume, without regularity assumptions on their boundaries.
item.dc:creator: Shibing Chen, Neil S. Trudinger, Xu-Jia Wang

item.title: Cavity collapse and kinetic energy concentration in three-dimensional free-boundary Euler flow
item.description: arXiv:2610.23605v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct smooth axisymmetric solutions of the three-dimensional incompressible free-boundary Euler equations in bounded domains for which a tubular cavity collapses onto a circle at a finite time $T$. The velocity has a single-valued potential, and the construction applies without surface tension and with any fixed positive surface tension. Both boundary components remain embedded and disjoint before collapse, while the outer boundary converges smoothly. The terminal outer meridional domain may be any smooth bounded simply connected domain whose closure is separated from the rotation axis; the interior point generating the collapse circle and the positive concentrated energy may be prescribed independently. We prove a sharp collapse law with radius asymptotic to an explicit multiple of $(T-t)^{1/2}|\log(T-t)|^{-1/4}$, determine curvature blow-up asymptotics, and show that kinetic energy concentrates uniformly on the circle. For a canonical reflection symmetric family, we identify a common cylindrical spacetime limit and sharp velocity and pressure profiles. At every fixed spatial point in the region enclosed by the limiting outer boundary and away from the collapse circle, the velocity tends to zero while the pressure tends to positive infinity. For this family, we characterize the topology of the limiting material map and prove its optimal $1/2$-H\"older regularity and sharp $W^{1,p}$ threshold $1\le p<2$, with first derivatives in weak $L^2$ but not in $L^2$. These canonical solutions admit weak continuations that preserve mass and momentum and whose total energy drops at collapse by exactly the concentrated kinetic energy.
item.dc:creator: Tao Luo, Siqi Yang

item.title: Asymptotic gradient regularity for degenerate or singular fully nonlinear parabolic equations
item.description: arXiv:2610.23683v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This is a continuation of our recent work~\cite{WZJ26} on asymptotic gradient regularity for nonlinear parabolic equations. In this paper, we consider bounded viscosity solutions of the degenerate or singular fully nonlinear parabolic equation \begin{equation*} u_t-|Du|^\gamma F(D^2u)=f \quad \text{in } Q_1, \end{equation*} where $ \gamma>-1 $, $ F $ is uniformly $ (\lambda, \Lambda)$-elliptic with $0<\lambda\leq\Lambda$, $F(0)=0$, and $f\in C^0(Q_1)\cap L^\infty(Q_1)$. Given any prescribed $\alpha\in(0,1)$, we prove that there exists $ \varepsilon=\varepsilon(n,\alpha)>0 $ such that \[ |\gamma|+\left(\frac{\Lambda}{\lambda}-1\right) \leq \varepsilon \quad \Longrightarrow \quad u \in C_{\mathrm{loc}}^{1+\alpha,\frac{1+\alpha}{2}}(Q_1). \] In particular, the spatial gradient H\"older exponent can be chosen arbitrarily close to $1$ as $ (\gamma, \frac{\Lambda}{\lambda}) \to (0,1) $. This provides a fully nonlinear counterpart to the asymptotic gradient regularity result established in~\cite{WZJ26}.
item.dc:creator: Jiangwen Wang

item.title: Dissipative solutions for fibred Wasserstein gradient flows of Cahn-Hilliard-type energies
item.description: arXiv:2610.23718v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study fourth-order evolution equations with a fibred Wasserstein gradient-flow structure, describing spatial transport of finitely many or a continuum of types. The driving Cahn-Hilliard-like energy combines a diagonal gradient contribution with nonlinear interactions between types. We prove subsequential convergence of the fibred Jordan-Kinderlehrer-Otto scheme to solutions satisfying an energy-dissipation inequality. For general type distributions, the absence of compactness in the type variable is addressed through defect-based solution concepts. On $\mathbb R^d, d\le 3$, we construct dissipative solutions satisfying an additional entropy-dissipation inequality. On smooth bounded domains in any space dimension, a coercivity estimate for the metric slope allows us to construct energy-dissipating solutions without relying on flow interchange, thereby covering non-convex domains endowed with the intrinsic length distance. In both cases, a variational comparison of the piecewise constant and De Giorgi interpolants yields a common limiting energy and strong convergence of the difference to zero without requiring strong compactness. For finitely many types, the defects vanish and the construction yields weak solutions. We further establish weak-strong uniqueness of dissipative solutions in every space dimension and of energy-dissipating solutions in dimensions $d\le5$. Combined with the respective existence results, this yields strong convergence of the variational approximations whenever a sufficiently regular, strictly positive solution exists.
item.dc:creator: Georg Heinze, Katharina Hopf, Matthias Liero

item.title: Asymptotic stability of a Bloch skyrmion for the Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert equation
item.description: arXiv:2610.23753v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove the asymptotic stability of isolated skyrmions under the flow of the two-dimensional Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert equation. We consider a micromagnetic energy functional involving the exchange energy, the Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction, and the Zeeman interaction. We are interested in the stability of chiral Bloch skyrmions, which are local minimizers of this energy. We prove that data in H2 which are near in the skyrmion in a slighlty stronger than H1 sense, converge with exponential rate, in H2, to the skyrmion, up to a change of gauge.
item.dc:creator: Jordan Berthoumieu, Rapha\"el C\^ote

item.title: Regularity Aspects of Temperature in Heat-Conducting Fluid Systems via De Giorgi Methods
item.description: arXiv:2610.23802v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper is concerned with the conditional H\"older regularity of the temperature for the heat-conducting compressible Navier-Stokes system, where the pressure takes a complete form that includes the Stefan-radiation correction. Under minimal assumptions on the density and velocity, we prove that any weak solution automatically exhibits H\"older continuity in the temperature component. This constitutes the main result of the work and is achieved by an application of the De Giorgi method. As a consequence of this conditional regularity, we establish the global-in-time existence of a regular, unique solution to a simplified system for the compressible potential flow of a heat-conducting fluid, valid for arbitrarily large initial data.
item.dc:creator: Nilasis Chaudhuri, Piotr B. Mucha, Tomasz Piasecki, Jiakun Yang

item.title: Memory effects in the homogenization of a viscous fluid containing elastic particles
item.description: arXiv:2610.23819v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This work deals with a fluid-structure interaction problem involving an incompressible viscous fluid and a periodic array of tiny elastic inclusions in a three-dimensional domain. We focus on a critical regime where the volume fraction of the inclusions tends to zero, but their density and stiffness are scaled so that they still influence the macroscopic behavior. The asymptotic regime depends on the parameter $\gamma=\lim_{\varepsilon\to 0}r_\varepsilon/\varepsilon^3\in [0,+\infty]$, where $\varepsilon$ is the period and $r_\varepsilon$ the inclusion size. For $\gamma=0$ the solid and fluid equations uncouple in the limit. For $\gamma\in (0,+\infty]$, we show that the macroscopic fluid velocity satisfies a Stokes system with memory: the standard Stokes equations are augmented by convolution-in-time terms arising from the elastic vibrations of the inclusions. The existence of the convolution kernels is established for both $\gamma\in(0,+\infty)$ and $\gamma=\infty$ using semigroup theory. For $\gamma=\infty$ the microscopic problem reduces to a purely conservative elastodynamic equation and the kernels can be computed explicitly via spectral decomposition. They are oscillatory and almost-periodic in time, yielding a persistent, non-decaying memory. For $\gamma\in(0,+\infty)$ the microscopic elastodynamic equation is coupled to a local Stokes problem, whose viscous dissipation yields memory kernels that decay to zero at infinity.
item.dc:creator: J. Casado-D\'{\i}az, A. R. Hormigo-Molina

item.title: Uniform restriction lower bounds and nongeodesic common nodal curves in integrable systems
item.description: arXiv:2610.23836v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct a family of real analytic metrics on the two-torus, for which a fixed embedded nongeodesic circle is a nodal component of infinitely many real Laplace eigenfunctions. The examples address a question asked by Bourgain-Rudnick \cite{BR11}, and give a negative answer to the question asked by Toth-Zelditch \cite{TZ21} and Han \cite{Han}: whether a curve shared by infinitely many nodal sets must be geodesic. To explain the restriction obstruction, we prove uniform $L^2$ lower bounds for joint eigenfunctions of quantum completely integrable (QCI) systems under transverse crossing and isolation of a tangential characteristic branch, then extend to multi-branch setting. The results are used to characterize the possible joint nodal curves in the Liouville tori, narrowing down the choices. Finally, the counterexample realizes one possibility for which cancellation happens exactly on a nongeodesic curve.
item.dc:creator: Xianchao Wu, Xiao Xiao

item.title: Geometric Viewpoint of $L^\infty$ Estimates for Linearized Monge-Amp\`ere Equations
item.description: arXiv:2610.23848v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove a Harnack inequality on Monge--Amp\`ere gradient graphs under suitable geometric bounds, giving us interior $L^\infty$ estimates for the linearized Monge--Amp\`ere equation. The proof combines Moser iteration on extrensic balls with a gradient estimate for the extrinsic distance function. The argument avoids the Caffarelli--Guti\'errez Harnack inequality and the engulfing and covering properties of Monge--Amp\`ere sections.
item.dc:creator: Arghya Rakshit, Derek Wu

item.title: Remarks on prescribed scalar curvature functions
item.description: arXiv:2610.19667v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: This short article is devoted to the study of the positive solution of Yamabe-type semi-linear equation with prescribed coefficient on general closed manifolds. Our main result is to provide some sufficient conditions for the existence of the positive solutions and give some examples to show that those conditions are sharp. An application to scalar-flat manifold settles a long standing question in prescribing scalar curvature problem in negative form.
item.dc:creator: Mingxiang Li, Quoc Anh Ngo, Xingwang Xu

item.title: On the tradeoff between robustness and geometric accuracy in adversarial training
item.description: arXiv:2610.22955v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For non-parametric binary classification in the presence of an adversary, we prove an optimal quantitative estimate for adversarial classifiers controlling geometric accuracy, as measured by the Hausdorff distance to the Bayes classifier, in terms or their robustness, as encoded by the adversarial budget $\varepsilon$. This rigorously shows that robust classifiers sacrifice at most $O(\sqrt{\varepsilon})$ or $O(\varepsilon)$ in accuracy, depending on the regularity of the underlying Bayes classifier. In contrast to prior work on the incompatibility of robustness and accuracy over low-complexity hypothesis classes, our work shows that high-complexity hypothesis classes allow for robust classifiers with precisely quantified accuracy. Our results apply for adversaries determined by any norm on Euclidean space and in both the infinite and finite data settings.
item.dc:creator: Rachel Morris, Ryan Murray, Kerrek Stinson

item.title: Stochastic Shockwave Dynamics in First-Order Traffic Flow
item.description: arXiv:2610.23022v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Moving congestion fronts vary across realizations even when the traffic-flow law is fixed. This paper develops a generator-based formulation of the Lighthill--Whitham--Richards (LWR) model with random initial density and a deterministic fundamental diagram. Randomness enters through the initial spatial density field; every realization follows the same conservation law. For a smooth strictly concave fundamental diagram, we adapt established one-sided spatial Markov closure to traffic variables under the stated spatial-process and regularity assumptions, and derive a kinetic balance for physically normalized front intensities. Evolving the spatial generator provides density laws and congestion-front statistics without solving a road-grid problem for every realization. The formulation is continuous in physical space and time, while its numerical implementation approximates density state and integrates physical time. Four experiments distinguish deterministic consistency from stochastic comparison. Riemann and signal examples recover independently constructed exact LWR solutions. Smooth strictly concave approximations approach the deterministic triangular-diagram signal solution over the tested finite horizons; this does not establish stochastic closure at contacts or the capacity kink. A matched Monte Carlo Godunov ensemble evaluates front counts, sizes, mergers, and density distributions. The evolved generator also yields an instantaneous travel-time distribution for a frozen density field, compared with the same functional of the matched Godunov profiles. This quantity is not experienced travel time through evolving traffic. Resolution checks identify remaining normalization and small-front-loss effects. The contribution is direct evolution and interpretation of traffic-state and front distributions under a fixed first-order traffic law.
item.dc:creator: Yanlin Zhang, Alireza Talebpour

item.title: Improved $L^p$ maximal estimates for higher-degree Weyl sums
item.description: arXiv:2610.23379v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For each integer $k\ge3$, we establish the following estimate for all $1\le p<\infty$ and $\varepsilon>0$: \[ \left\|\sup_{t\in\mathbb{T}}\left|\sum_{n=1}^N e(nx+n^kt)\right|\right\|_{L^p(\mathbb{T})} \ll_{k,p,\varepsilon} N^{\max\{1-1/K_k,\,1-1/p\}+\varepsilon}, \] where $K_k=\min\{2^{k-1},k(k+1)/2\}$, $e(z)=e^{2\pi iz}$, and $\mathbb{T}=\mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z}$. For $k\ge5$, this improves our earlier bound \cite{chen-miao-yuan-zhao} for $1\le p<D_k$, where $D_k=\min\{2^{k-1},k(k-1)\}$, and, together with the corresponding lower bound, extends the sharp range up to $N^\varepsilon$ from $p\ge D_k$ to $p\ge K_k$. The main new ingredient is a mixed minor-arc moment estimate obtained before taking the time supremum. The minor-arc maximal estimate then follows from a smooth reproducing kernel argument, while the major arcs are handled directly by Poisson summation and classical complete exponential-sum estimates. The reduction from suprema to mean values also yields a short and direct proof of improved $L^p$ estimates for maximal operators on Weyl sums with general polynomial phases, strengthening \cite[Theorem 1.1]{baker-chen-shparlinski}.
item.dc:creator: Xuezhi Chen, Changxing Miao, Jiye Yuan, Tengfei Zhao

item.title: Complete harmonic metrics and subharmonic functions on the complex plane
item.description: arXiv:2610.23441v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: This paper continues our previous work \cite{Miy6} on an extension of the Li--Mochizuki theorem concerning the existence and uniqueness of complete diagonal harmonic metrics on cyclic Higgs bundles over open Riemann surfaces. We consider the extended Hitchin equation associated with general subharmonic weight functions on the canonical bundle, not necessarily induced by holomorphic $r$-differentials. We establish uniqueness of complete solutions with determinant $1$ for arbitrary subharmonic weight functions, without additional regularity assumptions on them. We also prove that, on the complex plane, such a complete solution exists whenever the weight function is not identically $-\infty$. Furthermore, if $(\varphi_\epsilon)_{\epsilon>0}$ is a family of smooth subharmonic weight functions decreasing to such a weight function $\varphi$ as $\epsilon\searrow0$, the associated family of smooth complete solutions $(h_\epsilon)_{\epsilon>0}$ with $\det(h_\epsilon)=1$ converges monotonically to the unique complete solution $h$ associated with $\varphi$ and satisfying $\det(h)=1$.
item.dc:creator: Natsuo Miyatake

item.title: Height of minimal surfaces: sharp thresholds
item.description: arXiv:2610.23629v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The confinement theorem of [CM1] gives Euclidean volume growth for a proper minimal submanifold whose height over a plane is sublinear. Such volume growth places strong restrictions on the geometry. This leaves linear height as the natural borderline and raises the question of which, if any, linearly growing cones still force Euclidean growth. Here we determine this borderline sharply for proper holomorphic curves in $C^2$. There are two sharp thresholds for the aperture depending on the K\"ahler angle $\theta$ of the two-plane $\Pi$: $\tan(\theta/2)$ and $\cot(\theta/2)$. No proper holomorphic curve exists below the first, every such curve is algebraic below the second, and superquadratic proper holomorphic disks exist above the second. These conclusions extend to holomorphic submanifolds of arbitrary dimension and codimension. For stationary integral varifolds there are again three regimes: sublinear height forces Euclidean growth, narrow cones of aperture $\varepsilon$ force polynomial growth with exponent $n+O(\varepsilon^2)$, and wide cones allow arbitrarily fast growth. The order $\varepsilon^2$ is sharp: already in $R^3$, for every small $\varepsilon>0$ there are examples in a cone of aperture $\varepsilon$ whose volume grows at least like $r^{2+\frac45\varepsilon^2}$.
item.dc:creator: Tobias Holck Colding, William P. Minicozzi II

item.title: Three-circle inequalities for almost harmonic functions on cylinders
item.description: arXiv:2610.23648v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The three-circle method was introduced into the blow-up analysis of harmonic maps by Qing and Tian [Comm. Pure Appl. Math. 1997]. We extend this method to a class of $(\tau,\epsilon)$-almost harmonic functions on long cylinders and establish three-circle inequalities for their weighted energies. These inequalities yield a dichotomy between exponential energy decay and asymptotic dominance of a critical Fourier mode, together with a characterization of the corresponding normalized limiting profiles. In the unweighted case, we prove convergence of the averaged neck curves and identify their limiting equations under additional structural assumptions. Applications include neck analysis and energy identities for harmonic maps, solutions of Rivi\`ere's equation, $\alpha$-harmonic maps, biharmonic approximations of harmonic maps, and Willmore surfaces.
item.dc:creator: Yuxiang Li, Wenjuan Qi

item.title: Exponential convergence to a steady-state for a population genetics model with sexual reproduction and selection
item.description: arXiv:2104.06089v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We are interested in the dynamics of a population structured by a phenotypic trait. Individuals reproduce sexually, which is represented by a non-linear integral operator. This operator is combined to a multiplicative operator representing selection. When the strength of selection is small, we show that the dynamics of the population is governed by a simple macroscopic differential equation, and that solutions converge exponentially to steady-states that are locally unique. The analysis is based on Wasserstein distance inequalities using a uniform lower bound on distributions. These inequalities are coupled to tail estimates to show the stability of the steady-states.
item.dc:creator: Ga\"el Raoul

item.title: Quantitative Schauder estimates for hypoelliptic equations
item.description: arXiv:2305.00463v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We derive Schauder estimates using ideas from Campanato's approach for a general class of local hypoelliptic operators and non-local kinetic equations. The method covers equations in divergence and non-divergence form. In particular our results are applicable to the inhomogeneous Landau and to the non-cutoff Boltzmann equation. The paper is self-contained.
item.dc:creator: Am\'elie Loher

item.title: Scaling-Critical Theory for the Boltzmann and Landau Equations
item.description: arXiv:2509.14845v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This paper develops a scaling-critical theory for the spatially inhomogeneous non-cutoff Boltzmann and Landau equations with very soft potentials. For sufficiently small initial perturbations in a localized, weighted, anisotropic Riesz-potential norm, we prove global well-posedness near a Maxwellian in the whole space. This critical phase-space norm captures the Boltzmann--Landau scaling, the velocity-dependent anisotropy, and the hypoelliptic transport structure. The proof combines frozen-operator estimates, a critical fixed-point argument, and weighted hypocoercive energy estimates. We also develop a short-time pointwise Green-function theory for variable-coefficient kinetic equations with a nonnegative H\"older background. We first construct the small-jump Green function by freezing coefficients along kinetic characteristics and then recover the full kernel through a convergent parametrix expansion. The resulting bounds capture the fractional Kolmogorov geometry near characteristics and rapid decay away from them. These estimates form the analytic core of the scaling-critical theory and provide a robust pointwise framework for further regularity analysis in the soft-potential regime.
item.dc:creator: Ke Chen, Quoc-Hung Nguyen, Tong Yang

item.title: Nonlinear effects of incoming time-periodic boundary conditions on shock waves for scalar conservation laws
item.description: arXiv:2510.26153v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This paper is concerned with the large-time behavior of inviscid and viscous shocks for scalar conservation laws on the half-line $(-\infty,0)$ under an incoming \emph{time-periodic} boundary condition. This problem arises naturally from classical piston problems in fluid mechanics. Even for arbitrarily small periodic oscillations of the boundary data, the effect of the boundary manifests itself through a persistent time-periodic component near the boundary, which behaves as a \emph{boundary wave}. For inviscid shocks moving away from the boundary ($s<0$), this boundary wave repeatedly interacts with the shock over infinitely many periods. We show that the repeated interactions do not generate secular growth, but instead produce a finite \emph{cumulative} correction to the asymptotic shock location. For the inviscid stationary case $s=0$, the time-periodic boundary \emph{modulates} the background stationary shock into a genuinely time-periodic shock configuration, to which the solution converges. In the viscous case with $s<0$, the boundary wave couples with the viscous shock through a transitional region induced by diffusion, and the solution converges asymptotically to their superposition. Our results show that for scalar conservation laws, the persistent boundary wave modifies the shock without producing resonance.
item.dc:creator: Yuan Yuan

item.title: A Liouville theorem for convex functions with periodic Monge-Amp\`ere measure
item.description: arXiv:2511.15021v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study global convex solutions of the Monge-Amp\`ere equation \[ \det D^2 u = \mu \quad \text{in } \mathbb{R}^n, \] where $\mu \not\equiv 0$ is a nonnegative locally finite periodic Borel measure on $\mathbb{R}^n$. We prove a Liouville-type theorem showing that every such solution admits a unique decomposition, up to an additive constant, as the sum of a quadratic polynomial and a periodic function. This extends earlier results of Caffarelli-Li and Li-Lu, which required $\mu$ to have a density with regular or bounded logarithm, to the full generality of periodic measures, allowing degeneracy and singularities. A key ingredient is a new dichotomous Harnack-type inequality for linearized Monge-Amp\`ere equations with nonnegative periodic measures, which compensates for the failure of doubling and engulfing properties in the degenerate setting. In the extremal example where $\mu$ is the periodic Dirac measure supported on the integer lattice, we show that the solutions, up to addition of a linear function, are in one-to-one correspondence with Dirichlet-Voronoi tilings of $\mathbb{R}^n$.
item.dc:creator: Tianling Jin, YanYan Li, Hung V. Tran, Xushan Tu

item.title: Modal bases of coaxial electromagnetic step index fibers
item.description: arXiv:2603.16716v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We consider the eigenvalue problem to find the modes of an electromagnetic coaxial step index fiber. More specific, we consider a closed (meaning PEC boundary conditions) cylindrical waveguide with circular cross section $\Gamma$, wave propagation modeled by the time-harmonic Maxwell's equations with frequency $\omega$, the permeability $\mu$ and the permittivity $\epsilon$ being scalar, uniformly positive, piece-wise constant and depending only on the radial variable of the cross section. We prove that if the deviation from the homogeneous case is small, i.e., $\delta_{\epsilon,\mu}:=\|\epsilon-\epsilon_0\|_{L^\infty}+\|\mu-\mu_0\|_{L^\infty}<<1$, then the (appropriately scaled) tangential electric (magnetic) fields of the modes form Riesz bases in $\mathbf{H}_{0}(\operatorname{curl}_{\Gamma};\Gamma)$ ($\mathbf{H}(\operatorname{curl}_{\Gamma};\Gamma)$) and the natural trace space $\mathbf{H}_{0}^{-1/2}(\operatorname{curl}_{\Gamma};\Gamma)$ ($\mathbf{H}^{-1/2}(\operatorname{curl}_{\Gamma};\Gamma)$). These results hold also for complex frequencies $\omega$. In addition, if $\omega\in\mathbb{R}$, then for small enough $\delta_{\epsilon,\mu}$ all wavenumbers are located on the axes and there exist no backward modes. Key tools in the analysis are a particular reformulation of the eigenvalue problem, the perturbation theory for selfadjoint operators under a local subordinate condition and uniform properties of Bessel functions.
item.dc:creator: Martin Halla

item.title: Non-Existence of thick bubble rings at low Weber numbers
item.description: arXiv:2603.24217v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We examine the existence of thick bubble rings within the framework of the free-boundary capillary Euler equations, focusing on the regime of low Weber numbers. Although spheroidal bubbles are known to approach a spherical shape in this limit, the possibility of thick bubble rings persisting at low Weber numbers has remained uncertain. In contrast to the ordinary Euler equations, which admit thick vortex ring solutions, our analysis reveals that the free-boundary capillary Euler equations do not support thick bubble rings at low Weber numbers. This distinction highlights the significant impact of surface tension on the behavior of vortex rings in the capillary regime.
item.dc:creator: Yuanjiang Han, Christian Seis

item.title: Isolated Singularities for Fractional Hartree Equations
item.description: arXiv:2606.10990v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study isolated singularities of positive solutions to a fractional Hartree equation with Riesz interaction, \[ (-\Delta)^s u = \left( \int_{\mathbb{R}^N\setminus\{0\}} \frac{u^p(y)}{|x-y|^\mu}\,dy \right)u^q \quad \text{in } \mathbb{R}^N\setminus\{0\}. \] The puncture changes the passage from the differential equation to its integral form: a fractional fundamental solution term may occur at the singular point. Under an upper bound at the scale of the fundamental solution and a weighted integrability condition on the source, we derive a Riesz decomposition with a nonnegative singular term. Under the same assumptions, if in addition the solution blows up at the puncture, \(p,q\ge1\), and both Kelvin weights are nonnegative, an off-center moving spheres argument yields radial symmetry and strict radial decrease. We also classify positive radial homogeneous singular solutions under the corresponding convergence conditions. If a nonzero positive radial homogeneous scaling limit exists and solves the limiting equation, this classification uniquely determines its coefficient.
item.dc:creator: Guangze Gu, Aleks Jevnikar, Zhipeng Yang

item.title: Non-radial solutions for the quasi-linear H\'enon type $N$-Laplacian Liouville equation
item.description: arXiv:2607.24012v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we investigate the following quasi-linear weighted $N$-Laplacian Liouville equation \begin{equation*}\label{0} -\Delta_N u=|x|^{N\alpha}e^{u}, \qquad x\in \R^N, \end{equation*} where $N \geq 2$. For $\al>0$, by carefully studying the linearized problem and applying the approximation method and bifurcation theory, we prove that, when the parameter $\alpha$ equals to the critical values $\alpha(k):=\frac{\sqrt{k(N-1)(k+N-2)}}{N-1}-1$ for $k \geq 2$, there exist non-radial solutions $u$ (bifurcating from $U_{\alpha(k)}$) to the above quasi-linear H\'enon type Liouville equation such that $u\sim \ln|x|$, $|\nabla u|= O(|x|^{-1})$ at $\infty$ and $\int_{\R^N}|x|^{N\alpha}e^{u}\md x=N\left(\frac{N^2}{N-1}\right)^{N-1}(\alpha+1)^{N-1}\omega_N$. One should note that, $\alpha(k)=k-1$ for $k\geq2$ when $N=2$. Our results successfully extend the existence result of J. Prajapat and G. Tarantello in \cite{PT} concerning the $2$-dimension and Laplacian case (i.e., $N=2$) to the more general $N$-dimension and $N$-Laplacian cases ($N\geq 2$), and extend the results of F. Gladiali, M. Grossi, and S. L. N. Neves in \cite{GGN} and the authors in \cite{DDGL} from $1<p<N$ to the much more complicated limiting case $p=N$. We introduced some new ideas and overcame a series of crucial difficulties, including the nonlinearity nature of the $N$-Laplacian $\Delta_N$, the lack of Green integral representation formula and critical weighted Sobolev embedding inequality, the absence of Kelvin type transforms for linearized/difference equations, the invariance of the total mass under scalings of $u$, and the signs-changing and divergence (to $-\infty$) at $\infty$ of the solutions, which makes the suitable choices of the approximate problems, the (normalized) approximate function sequences and the working space to be quite difficult.
item.dc:creator: Wei Dai, Lixiu Duan, Changfeng Gui, Yuan Li

item.title: A partial answer to Brezis' Open Problem 2.1
item.description: arXiv:2608.21896v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we give a partial answer to Brezis' Open Problem~2.1, which concerns the uniqueness of solutions to the Ginzburg--Landau equation in the unit disc with the degree-one boundary condition. Let $\lambda_1$ be the first Dirichlet eigenvalue of $-\Delta$ in the unit disc and set $\varepsilon_*:=\lambda_1^{-1/2}$. We prove that there exists $\delta>0$ such that the radial solution is the unique weak solution for every $\varepsilon\in(\varepsilon_*-\delta,\infty)$. More generally, we establish the analogous uniqueness result for the Ginzburg--Landau system on bounded connected $C^{1,1}$ domains in $\mathbb R^N$, $2\leq N\leq4$, with nontrivial boundary data. In particular, uniqueness persists slightly below the convexity threshold $\varepsilon_*$, where the strict convexity argument is no longer available. The proof combines strict convexity for $\varepsilon\geq\varepsilon_*$ with a compactness argument, nondegeneracy of the solution at $\varepsilon=\varepsilon_*$ and the implicit function theorem.
item.dc:creator: Chao Ji, Kai Sheng

item.title: Inviscid damping without derivatives near Couette flow
item.description: arXiv:2608.24840v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the long-time dynamics near Couette flow for the 2D Euler equations in unbounded geometries. We identify a mechanism of nonlinear inviscid damping at Yudovich regularity, distinct from classical phase mixing: velocity decay driven by spatial evacuation of vorticity. The mechanism leads to a geometry-sign classification of the dynamics. In the infinite channel, small nonnegative bounded-vorticity perturbations undergo global damping without derivative assumptions. In the whole plane, small nonnegative perturbations exhibit enhanced dispersion and velocity damping, while non-positive perturbations remain confined and do not damp, even when arbitrarily small in Gevrey classes. Moreover, damping can coexist with infinite-time growth of vorticity derivatives, even under arbitrary shear modulation. The classification is obtained through an interplay between new Lyapunov functionals and Hamiltonian conservation.
item.dc:creator: Dengjun Guo, Xiaoyutao Luo

item.title: The capillary $L_p$ dual Minkowski problem for $p>q$ in higher dimensions
item.description: arXiv:2609.07158v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove that the capillary $L_p$ dual Minkowski problem in $\mathbb{R}^{n+1}$, $n\geq3$, admits a unique positive smooth strictly convex solution for any prescribed positive smooth function $f$ when $p>q$ and the contact angle satisfies $\theta\in(0,\pi/2)$. Earlier results for $p>q$ either required the additional condition $q\leq1$ or were restricted to $n=2$. We reduce the problem to a Monge--Amp\`ere type equation with a Robin boundary condition on a spherical cap. By constructing a new auxiliary function for the global $C^2$ estimate, we overcome these limitations and completely resolve the case of $p>q$ in higher dimensions, i.e., prove existence and uniqueness throughout the case of $p>q$, without any further restriction on $p$ or $q$.
item.dc:creator: Ya Gao

item.title: Explicit diagonalization of the linearized Calder\'on problem on the disk: multiplicity normalization and exponential spectral attenuation
item.description: arXiv:2609.23740v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the full angular dependence of the linearized Schr\"odinger form of the Calder\'on problem on the unit disk. We obtain an explicit continuous spectral diagonalization of its normal operator and hence a generalized singular system for the linearized forward map. To our knowledge, this is the first such diagonalization for the full angularly dependent, multiplicity-normalized linearized measurement map on the disk.
item.dc:creator: William Robert Breckon Lionheart

item.title: Isothermal hydrodynamic limit for kinetic flocking models with nonlinear velocity alignment
item.description: arXiv:2609.30457v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the hydrodynamic limit of kinetic flocking models with nonlinear velocity alignment and strong local Fokker--Planck forcing. In the limit of small Knudsen number the kinetic densities converge to a local Maxwellian centered around macroscopic quantities satisfying the compressible Euler system with isothermal pressure $p = \s \rho$, while macroscopic alignment is obtained by convolution of the microscopic velocity law with the standard Gaussian, resulting in a different nonlinearity. Such discrepancy has been observed already in \cite{black2025hydrodynamic}. In this note we rigorously justify the limit for admissible weak kinetic solutions and non-vacuous limiting macroscopic solution. Our analysis provides a quantitative rate of convergence in terms of relative entropy: $\cH(f_\e | \mu) \lesssim \e$ provided initially $\cH(f_\e(0) | \mu(0)) \leq \e$. In the linear case we recover the known result \cite{karper2015hydrodynamic}.
item.dc:creator: Roman Shvydkoy, Changhui Tan

item.title: Hessian Estimates for Convex Solutions of Hessian Quotient Equations via Compactness
item.description: arXiv:2610.08442v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We give a compactness proof of interior Hessian estimates for convex solutions of $\sigma_n(D^2u)/\sigma_{n-2}(D^2u)=1$ and $\sigma_n(D^2u)/\sigma_{n-1}(D^2u)=f(x,u,Du)>0$, with $1/f$ concave in the gradient variable in the latter case, revisiting results of Lu and Fung.
item.dc:creator: Jianxiang Liu

item.title: Stability for a formally determined Lorentzian inverse problem
item.description: arXiv:2610.10413v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We consider the inverse problem of recovering a potential $q$, depending on space and time, in the wave equation $(\Box_g+q)u=0$ on a Lorentzian manifold. We prove Lipschitz stability for a formally determined version of this problem under a \textit{null-cone foliation} assumption. As a consequence, we obtain uniqueness for the Lorentzian Calder\'on problem in a fixed conformal class. Our approach uses distorted spherical waves.
item.dc:creator: Spyridon Filippas, Lauri Oksanen

item.title: Negative Sobolev regularity and optimal decay for the fractional Navier--Stokes--Poisson system
item.description: arXiv:2610.15594v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We establish global well-posedness and sharp higher-order decay estimates for the fractional compressible Navier--Stokes--Poisson system in $\R^{3}$ with fractional Lam\'e--Navier dissipation $\Lame^\alpha u$ with $\alpha\in[1/2,1]$, and Riesz coupling $\Lambda^{2\beta}\phi=\rho-\bar{\rho}$ with $\beta\in[0,1]$, where $\Lambda:=(-\Delta)^{1/2}$ and $\bar{\rho}>0$ denotes the constant background density. For small perturbations of a constant equilibrium in $H^{N\alpha}$ with $N\geq3$ and $N\alpha>5/2$, we prove the global existence and uniqueness of classical solutions. Furthermore, we propagate the negative Sobolev norms with uniform-in-time bounds and derive the higher-order decay estimates, provided that the initial perturbation additionally belongs to $\dot{H}^{-\vartheta}$ for some $\vartheta\in[0,3/2)$. Moreover, we establish the optimality of these decay rates within the prescribed initial data class for the velocity and the Riesz potential in their natural energy norms. The density decay exponents are also optimal whenever the available regularity permits the full Riesz-induced gain. The analysis relies on a nonlinear energy structure adapted to both fractional dissipation and Riesz interaction, together with Sobolev interpolation. The optimality of the decay is proved by constructing smooth initial data localized at low frequencies and proving matching upper and lower decay bounds for the resulting solutions. These solutions show that the low-frequency linear dynamics including the Riesz-induced density gain, persists under nonlinear evolution.
item.dc:creator: Yuan Xu, Junhao Zhang

item.title: Uniform $L^2$-bounds for the $n$-th Calder\'on commutator on Lipschitz graphs
item.description: arXiv:2610.20489v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove that, for every real Lipschitz function $A$ and every integer $n\ge1$, $\|T_{A,n}\|_{L^2(\mathbb{R})\to L^2(\mathbb{R})}\le C\,\|A'\|_\infty^n$, where $T_{A,n}$ is the $n$-th Calder\'on commutator and $C$ is an absolute constant. The essential tool is the Coifman--McIntosh--Meyer theorem, applied to a holomorphic family of complex curves, together with the Cauchy integral formula on a contour surrounding the interval of secant slopes. We also include a simpler version of the argument that yields an $O(\log n)$ bound and motivates the choice of contour.
item.dc:creator: Joan Hern\'andez, Joan Mateu, Laura Prat

item.title: A class of sum Hessian quotient equations arising in conformal geometry
item.description: arXiv:2610.21106v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we investigate the existence result of $(n-1)$-admissible solutions to a class of sum Hessian quotient equations with the modified Schouten tensor on Riemannian manifolds. By establishing uniform a priori estimates, we prove the solvability of the problem via degree theory.
item.dc:creator: Ni Xiang, Yuni Xiong

item.title: Training-Induced Escape from Token Clustering in a Mean-Field Formulation of Transformers
item.description: arXiv:2605.07772v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Transformers perform inference by iteratively transforming token representations across layers. This layerwise computation has been studied empirically, and recent mean-field theories of Transformer dynamics explain how attention can drive token distributions toward clustering. However, existing analyses treat model parameters as prescribed, leaving open how training reshapes this clustering picture. We study this question in a noisy mean-field Transformer in which only a parameter-linear FFN is trained under $L^2$ regularization. We identify a training-induced phase of the inference dynamics across layers: after clustering in the early layers, the token distribution can leave the clustered regime near the final layers. A single gradient-descent update already produces this escape, and minimizers of the training objective satisfy an exponential turnpike bound under which clustering persists through the interior layers. Our analysis is based on an entropy-regularized interaction energy that captures the clustering bias of attention, for which we establish a double-well landscape and a local Polyak-{\L}ojasiewicz inequality. More broadly, our results point toward a training-aware mean-field theory in which training and inference dynamics of Transformers are treated together.
item.dc:creator: Noboru Isobe, Daisuke Inoue, Masaaki Imaizumi

item.title: Ideal G{\aa}rding polynomials
item.description: arXiv:2607.16832v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We introduce ideal G{\aa}rding polynomials, a convexity-enhanced subclass of G\aa{}rding polynomials whose G{\aa}rding components are recursively convex under partial differentiation. This class strictly contains real stable polynomials and, after translation and homogenization, lies in the Lorentzian class. Our main result is that ideal G{\aa}rding polynomials still admit a robust structure theory despite this additional convexity: they are preserved under polarization, satisfy natural closure properties, and support a linear preserver theory. A key contribution of this paper is a universal model for univariate G{\aa}rding polynomials, described by monotone root sequences and equivalently by volume polynomials of Pitman--Stanley polytopes. We establish quotient concavity, and Newton--Maclaurin type inequalities, which leads to the polarization theorem, and suggests further connections with convex geometry and Lorentzian polynomials.
item.dc:creator: Hao Fang, Biao Ma

item.title: Uniform logarithmic Sobolev inequalities for the 2D Coulomb gas at the diffusive temperature scale
item.description: arXiv:2608.24863v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: For $N\ge2$ and $\beta>0$, consider the canonical 2D Coulomb gas ensemble \begin{equation} \mathrm{d}\mathbb{P}_{N,\beta}(Z) =\mathsf{Z}_{N,\beta}^{-1}e^{-\beta|Z|^2/2} \prod_{i<j}|z_i-z_j|^{\beta/N}\mathrm{d} Z \qquad\text{on }\mathbb{C}^N. \end{equation} The factor $N^{-1}$ in the pair exponent places the ensemble at the diffusive, or high-temperature, scale. We prove that, for every fixed inverse temperature $\beta>0$, this Gibbs measure satisfies a logarithmic Sobolev inequality (LSI) on the closed Dirichlet-form domain generated by collision-free compactly supported smooth functions, with a positive constant independent of $N$. The LSI constant may be chosen uniformly when $\beta$ ranges over a compact subset of $(0,\infty)$. A second main result establishes Poincar\'e and logarithmic Sobolev inequalities for planar Gaussian measures weighted by finite products of positive powers of distances to points, with constants depending only on the total variance of the underlying Gaussian measure and the total exponent, not on the number or locations of the points. To prove the full labeled Poincar\'e inequality, we decompose variance into permutation-invariant and label-dependent parts, controlled respectively by a weighted $\bar\partial$ estimate and by relative-coordinate conditioning with random transpositions; separately, one-site logarithmic Sobolev inequalities, a conditional entropy inequality, and a repulsive partition estimate give a defective logarithmic Sobolev inequality. Rothaus tightening combines the resulting full labeled Poincar\'e inequality with the defective logarithmic Sobolev inequality. The two main theorems on their stated closed form domains and all results used in their formal proofs, including those from the literature, have been formalized in Lean 4.
item.dc:creator: Matthew Rosenzweig

item.title: Asymptotic analysis of an optimal control problem for a phase field tumor growth model with hyperbolic relaxation of the chemical potential
item.description: arXiv:2610.04380v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this paper, we study the optimal control of a phase field tumor growth model of Cahn--Hilliard type with possibly singular potential in which the often assumed parabolic relaxation of the chemical potential is replaced by a hyperbolic one. We investigate the asymptotic behavior of the control problem as the relaxation parameter $\,\alpha\,$ approaches zero. It is shown that the corresponding state and adjoint state variables of the relaxed problem converge in a suitable sense to their counterparts for the unrelaxed regime where $\alpha=0$. Also, weak limits of optimal controls for the relaxed problem can be shown to be optimal controls for the unrelaxed case. Moreover, every fixed optimal control $\,u^*\,$ for the unrelaxed system turns out to be the limit of a family $\{u^*_\alpha\}_{\alpha>0}$ of minimizers of suitable optimal control problems for the relaxed systems, where the original cost functional is replaced by the so-called ``adapted'' cost functional. It is also shown that the variational inequalities satisfied by $u^*_\alpha$, which constitute the first-order necessary optimality conditions of the relaxed problems with adapted cost functional, converge to the corresponding variational inequality fulfilled by $u^*$ for the unrelaxed problem with the original (nonadapted) cost functional.
